Credit checks stay in Acumatica: Once a kitchen's app order is in Acumatica, it still checks the customer's credit limit before releasing it, as it does for any order. Customer records, stock and invoicing remain there too. On our side sit each kitchen's guide and its prices, which you edit yourself, plus a copy of the orders chefs send with the app.

Kitchens on the portal stay there: A kitchen content with the Acumatica portal keeps its login and goes on ordering there. The app is for the ones who call instead, and an order a chef sends from it carries our order number and time stamp, which a call never gets.

Acumatica's app stays with your staff: Acumatica's own mobile app is made for your staff, who use it for sales orders and approvals. Ours goes on the kitchen's phone for one job only: getting the chef's reviewed order to you.

@graph.name: From your export to a kitchen's first order
@graph.description: Setup happens outside Acumatica, in three steps.

step.name: Pull a report from Acumatica
step.text: An Excel export listing each account's products, prices and your item codes is usually all we need.

step.name: Guides go live, account by account
step.text: We build the guides and set up the accounts, and each kitchen installs the app from its phone's store. Most place their first order the same day.

step.name: Checked orders land with your team
step.text: An order sent in the app arrives approved by the customer, numbered and time-stamped, in the format you picked.

@graph.name: Do we need an Acumatica alternative before kitchens can place spoken orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Keep Acumatica and its portal running, and hand our app to the chefs who pick the phone over a login. Acumatica still handles the money, the stock and the credit checks; the app lets those callers send a checked order without dialing.

@graph.name: Acumatica does not charge per user seat. Why not just give every kitchen a portal login?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can, and for kitchens that like to shop online it works well: live stock, their own prices, past orders to repeat. The gap is the kitchen that will not sit down to browse. For that kitchen, we offer a way to say what it needs instead.

@graph.name: Is talking an order through better than Acumatica's portal?

acceptedAnswer.text: For the kitchens that keep calling instead of logging in, yes: saying the order and checking each line suits them better than browsing a catalog and checking out. For kitchens happy in the portal, keep the portal. Either way, nothing moves out of Acumatica; our app sits alongside it and is not an Acumatica alternative.

@graph.name: Does anyone else sell voice add-ons for Acumatica?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Some add-ons let reps dictate orders. Others answer a customer's call and record what is ordered. Ours puts the app in the kitchen's hands, and the kitchen confirms every line before it reaches you.

@graph.name: Will orders flow into Acumatica on their own?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nothing links them out of the box: they are two products from two companies, and each company's support covers its own product only. Over EDI or through the API, the order may load straight into Acumatica without being typed again, if your system is set up to accept it; we check that in the demo. By email, you get a file the chef has already gone over, and your team enters it from that, not from a call or a voicemail.

@graph.name: Does our Acumatica partner have to be involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not to get started. Setup takes no Acumatica login and puts nothing inside it: we work from a spreadsheet you export. If orders should later import on their own, we cover in the demo what you would have to arrange.

@graph.name: How quickly could kitchens start, and what is the cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors are up and running in 24 to 48 hours, since nothing changes inside Acumatica. On price, Acumatica publishes a starting figure for its distribution package; we publish none and quote per distributor. An Acumatica replacement would shift your accounting, inventory and warehouse onto a new ERP, which is a different decision from adding an ordering app.
